name: Rail & Trucking
one_liner: Moving freight over land by railroad and truck, where rail wins on long-haul bulk cost efficiency and trucking wins on speed and flexibility.
how_it_makes_money: Railroads charge per carload or container, with pricing power from a concentrated network of few Class I carriers. Truckload carriers charge per mile, less-than-truckload (LTL) carriers charge per hundredweight for consolidated shipments, and both add fuel surcharges. Revenue mixes contract rates with more volatile spot rates.
revenue_formula: Rail revenue = carloads × revenue per carload
Truckload revenue = trucks × loaded miles per truck × rate per mile
LTL revenue = shipments × weight per shipment × revenue per hundredweight
cost_structure: Labor: drivers and crews; the largest cost for trucking
Fuel: partially passed through via surcharges
Track and network maintenance (rail): large fixed capex
Insurance and claims: rising for trucking
margins: Class I railroads typically run operating ratios around roughly 60-65%, one of the most profitable transport modes. Truckload carriers earn thin, cyclical margins in a fragmented market, while LTL is more consolidated and more profitable. Network density and freight cycle drive the spread.

key_metrics.name: Operating ratio (OR)
key_metrics.what: Operating expenses divided by revenue; lower is better and it is the headline metric for rails and truckers.

key_metrics.name: Deadhead / empty miles
key_metrics.what: Share of miles driven without cargo, a key efficiency drag.

key_metrics.name: Asset utilization (miles per tractor)
key_metrics.what: How productively fleet capital is used.

key_metrics.name: Train velocity and dwell time
key_metrics.what: Rail network speed and service quality.

trends: Prolonged freight recession with excess truck capacity pressuring rates
Rail consolidation, including the proposed Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern merger
Precision scheduled railroading and debates over service levels
Intermodal competing to win long-haul truck freight
Driver shortages, autonomous trucking pilots and electrification
Nearshoring driving cross-border freight with Mexico

case_angles.question: A trucking company's operating ratio worsened; how do you fix it?
Should two Class I railroads merge?
How can a railroad win more freight from trucks?
Should a truckload carrier invest in autonomous trucks?

interview_hooks: Does precision scheduled railroading create long-term value or just short-term margin at the expense of service?
Will a transcontinental railroad merger help or hurt shippers?
When will autonomous trucking become economically meaningful?
